en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn how fluent speakers avoid saying the same thing twice: short replies like *I think so* and *I hope not*, **do so**, **one** and **ones**, and leaving out words everyone already understands. Let's start!

steps.title: Say it once
steps.text: You already do this! *Me too*, *Yes, I do*, *I'd love to* and *the red one* all avoid repeating words.
steps.body:
English doesn't like repeating. There are two tools:
- **substitution**: replace words already said with a short word: *so, not, one, ones, do so*. *Is the shop open? I think **so**.* (so = the shop is open)
- **ellipsis**: leave out words that are already clear: *I'd like **to**, but I **can't**.* (= I'd like to come, but I can't come)
Indonesian can drop almost everything (*Bisa? Bisa.*). English usually keeps **one small word**: *so*, *one*, *to* or the auxiliary.

pairs.id: mengganti kata yang sudah disebut dengan kata pendek
anak kalimat (subjek + kata kerja: the shop is open)
kata kerja bantu (be, do, did, have, can, will, might…)

steps.title: so and not: a whole idea in one word
steps.text: After some verbs, **so** = a 'yes' idea and **not** = a 'no' idea. They replace the whole clause.
steps.body:
Verbs: **think, believe, expect, suppose, guess, hope, be afraid**.
- yes → **so**: *I think so. I hope so.*
- no with think / believe / expect → **I don't think so** (*I think not* is correct but formal and rare).
- no with hope / be afraid → only **not**: *I hope not*, never 'I don't hope so'.
**be afraid + so / not** = polite bad news (*sayangnya*), not fear.
Trap: *saya kira iya / semoga tidak* → 'I think **yes**', 'I hope **no**' ✗. Never yes, no or it here.

steps.title: The last train
steps.text: It's almost midnight at Manggarai station in Jakarta. The last KRL to Bogor left ten minutes ago. A tourist asks you something. Press play and listen.

question.listen: Excuse me, has the last train to Bogor already left?
question.prompt: You work at a station in Jakarta. The last train to Bogor left ten minutes ago. Listen to the tourist's question. Choose the correct, polite reply.
options: I'm afraid not.
I'm afraid so.
I'm afraid yes.
question.explanation: The tourist asked if the last train **has already left**. It has, and that's bad news, so: **I'm afraid so** (= sadly, yes). *I'm afraid not* would mean it hasn't left. *I'm afraid yes* copies the Indonesian *sayangnya iya*: after *be afraid*, use **so**.

steps.title: The broken printer
steps.text: Dimas asks you: 'Is the printer on the third floor working again?' You believe it's still broken, but you aren't 100% sure.

options: I think no, but I'll check.
I don't think so, but I'll check.
I don't think, but I'll check.
question.explanation: Your idea is **no**, so with *think* English puts *not* on the verb and keeps **so**: **I don't think so**. *I think no* copies *saya kira tidak*, and *I don't think* without *so* leaves the idea missing.

steps.title: do so, one and ones
steps.text: Two more short words: one for repeated **actions**, one for repeated **things**.
steps.body:
**do so** replaces a repeated action in **formal** English: *If you wish to cancel, please **do so** 24 hours in advance.* In speech: **do it / do that**.
**one / ones** replace a **countable noun** (*kata benda yang bisa dihitung*) already mentioned:
- *This laptop is slow. I need a faster **one**.*
- *the **one** on the left, the blue **ones***
Trap: *yang merah* → **the red one**, not 'the red'.
No 'a one' without an adjective, and no *one* for uncountable nouns: *some advice*, never 'an advice one'.

steps.title: At work and in the shops
steps.text: Look at what **do so**, **do it**, **one** and **ones** replace in each sentence.
steps.body: **one** = one thing, **ones** = more than one. **do so** = formal; **do it / do that** = everyday.

examples.en: Passengers must show their tickets. Failure to do so may result in a fine.
examples.id: Penumpang wajib menunjukkan tiket. Jika tidak, bisa dikenai denda.

examples.en: The company promised to cut plastic waste, and it has done so.
examples.id: Perusahaan itu berjanji mengurangi sampah plastik, dan sudah melakukannya.

examples.en: Can you send the invoice today? Sure, I'll do it now.
examples.id: Bisa kirim invoice-nya hari ini? Bisa, saya kerjakan sekarang.

examples.en: These mangoes are sweeter than the ones we bought last week.
examples.id: Mangga ini lebih manis daripada yang kita beli minggu lalu.

examples.en: Which room is ours? The one at the end of the corridor.
examples.id: Ruangan kita yang mana? Yang di ujung lorong.

steps.title: Chairs for the meeting room
steps.text: Bu Ani is choosing chairs for the new meeting room at an office furniture shop in Surabaya.

question.prompt: Complete what Bu Ani says: 'The grey chairs are comfortable, but I prefer the black ___. They match the table.'
options: one
them
ones
question.explanation: *chairs* is plural and countable, and *They match* shows more than one, so: **the black ones**. *one* is singular, and *them* can't come after an adjective ('the black them' ✗).

steps.title: Leave it out, but keep the auxiliary
steps.text: The last tool: say less. Keep one small word and drop the rest.
steps.body:
After an **auxiliary** (be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should…), keep it and drop the rest:
*Are you coming? I **might**.* / *I didn't go, but Rina **did**.*
After **to**, keep *to* and drop the verb: *I'd like **to**, but I can't.*
Traps: 'but I couldn't **do**' ✗ (*tidak bisa* needs no *do*), 'Yes, I'd like.' ✗ → *Yes, I'd like **to***.
At the end, don't shorten: *I'm not ready, but Sari **is*** (not *Sari's*).

pairs.en: I didn't go, but Rina did.
pairs.id: Saya tidak pergi, tapi Rina pergi.

pairs.en: I wanted to help, but I couldn't.
pairs.id: Saya mau bantu, tapi tidak bisa.

pairs.en: I'd like to, but I can't.
I haven't read it, but Pak Hasan has.
pairs.id: Saya belum membacanya, tapi Pak Hasan sudah.

pairs.en: You don't have to come if you don't want to.
pairs.id: Kamu tidak harus datang kalau tidak mau.

steps.title: The Saturday workshop
steps.text: Sari's team asked her to join the Saturday workshop, but she had to take her mother to the hospital. On Monday she explains.

options: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
I wanted to come, but I couldn't do.
I wanted, but I couldn't come.
question.explanation: **I couldn't** is enough: the auxiliary stands for *couldn't come*. Adding *do* is the Indonesian *tapi tidak bisa* trap. And *want* needs its **to**: *I wanted **to***, not *I wanted*.

steps.title: A promise kept
steps.text: Bu Ani was worried that the report would be late. But Rina kept her promise.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Rina janji mengirim laporannya, dan dia memang mengirimnya.
question.solution: Rina promised to send the report, and she did.
question.explanation: **did** stands for *sent the report*: keep the past auxiliary and drop the rest. Repeating *she sent the report* is correct but heavy.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for your next meeting, email or chat!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Ellipsis & substitution
artifact.intro: Say it once. Replace repeated words with a short word (so, not, do so, one, ones), or leave them out and keep the auxiliary or to.
rows: think / believe / expect / suppose / guess + so
Is the bank open today? I think so.
I don't think / believe / expect so
Is the meeting cancelled? I don't believe so.
I hope so / I hope not (not: I don't hope so)
Will it rain at the wedding? I hope not.
I'm afraid so / I'm afraid not
Is the flight delayed? I'm afraid so.
Do you need a visa? If so, apply early.
do so / did so / has done so
Please do so 24 hours in advance.
The ones on the top shelf are cheaper.
I'd like to, but I can't.
tips: Never **yes / no / it** after think or hope: *I think so*, *I hope not*.
Keep the small word: **to** or the **auxiliary**. No extra *do*: *I couldn't* ✓, *I couldn't do* ✗.
**do so** sounds formal: use it in notices, reports and emails; in conversation say *do it / do that*.

examples.en: Is Pak Hasan in? I'm afraid not. He's in a meeting.
examples.id: Pak Hasan ada? Sayangnya tidak. Beliau sedang rapat.

examples.en: Which mangoes do you want? The yellow ones, please.
examples.id: Mau mangga yang mana? Yang kuning, ya.

examples.en: She said she'd call, and she did.
examples.id: Dia bilang akan menelepon, dan dia memang menelepon.

steps.title: Read and practise
steps.text: Want more? Two British Council C1 pages, each with two short tests: one on ellipsis, and one on avoiding repetition in writing (with do so).

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu akan belajar cara penutur yang lancar menghindari mengulang hal yang sama: jawaban pendek seperti *I think so* dan *I hope not*, **do so**, **one** dan **ones**, dan menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas bagi semua orang. Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Cukup sekali
steps.text: Kamu sebenarnya sudah melakukannya! *Me too*, *Yes, I do*, *I'd love to* dan *the red one* semuanya menghindari pengulangan kata.
steps.body:
Bahasa Inggris tidak suka mengulang. Ada dua alat:
- **substitution** (substitusi): mengganti kata yang sudah disebut dengan kata pendek: *so, not, one, ones, do so*. *Is the shop open? I think **so**.* (so = tokonya buka)
- **ellipsis** (elipsis): menghilangkan kata yang sudah jelas: *I'd like **to**, but I **can't**.* (= saya mau datang, tapi tidak bisa datang)
Bahasa Indonesia bisa menghilangkan hampir semuanya (*Bisa? Bisa.*). Bahasa Inggris biasanya menyisakan **satu kata kecil**: *so*, *one*, *to* atau kata kerja bantunya.

pairs.id: mengganti kata yang sudah disebut dengan kata pendek
anak kalimat (subjek + kata kerja: the shop is open)
kata kerja bantu (be, do, did, have, can, will, might…)

steps.title: so dan not: satu ide utuh dalam satu kata
steps.text: Setelah beberapa kata kerja, **so** = ide 'iya' dan **not** = ide 'tidak'. Keduanya menggantikan seluruh anak kalimat.
steps.body:
Kata kerjanya: **think, believe, expect, suppose, guess, hope, be afraid**.
- iya → **so**: *I think so. I hope so.*
- tidak dengan think / believe / expect → **I don't think so** (*I think not* benar, tapi formal dan jarang).
- tidak dengan hope / be afraid → hanya **not**: *I hope not*, tidak pernah 'I don't hope so'.
**be afraid + so / not** = kabar buruk yang sopan (*sayangnya*), bukan takut.
Jebakan: *saya kira iya / semoga tidak* → 'I think **yes**', 'I hope **no**' ✗. Jangan pakai yes, no atau it di sini.

steps.title: Kereta terakhir
steps.text: Sudah hampir tengah malam di Stasiun Manggarai, Jakarta. KRL terakhir ke Bogor berangkat sepuluh menit yang lalu. Seorang turis bertanya kepadamu. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: Excuse me, has the last train to Bogor already left?
question.prompt: Kamu bekerja di stasiun di Jakarta. Kereta terakhir ke Bogor sudah berangkat sepuluh menit yang lalu. Dengarkan pertanyaan turis itu. Pilih jawaban yang benar dan sopan.
options: I'm afraid not.
I'm afraid so.
I'm afraid yes.
question.explanation: Turis itu bertanya apakah kereta terakhir **sudah berangkat**. Memang sudah, dan itu kabar buruk, jadi: **I'm afraid so** (= sayangnya iya). *I'm afraid not* berarti keretanya belum berangkat. *I'm afraid yes* meniru *sayangnya iya*: setelah *be afraid*, pakai **so**.

steps.title: Printer yang rusak
steps.text: Dimas bertanya kepadamu: 'Is the printer on the third floor working again?' Kamu yakin printernya masih rusak, tapi tidak 100% pasti.

options: I think no, but I'll check.
I don't think so, but I'll check.
I don't think, but I'll check.
question.explanation: Idemu adalah **tidak**, jadi dengan *think* bahasa Inggris menaruh *not* pada kata kerjanya dan tetap memakai **so**: **I don't think so**. *I think no* meniru *saya kira tidak*, dan *I don't think* tanpa *so* membuat idenya hilang.

steps.title: do so, one dan ones
steps.text: Dua kata pendek lagi: satu untuk **tindakan** yang diulang, satu untuk **benda** yang diulang.
steps.body:
**do so** menggantikan tindakan yang diulang dalam bahasa Inggris **formal**: *If you wish to cancel, please **do so** 24 hours in advance.* Dalam percakapan: **do it / do that**.
**one / ones** menggantikan **countable noun** (*kata benda yang bisa dihitung*) yang sudah disebut:
- *This laptop is slow. I need a faster **one**.*
- *the **one** on the left, the blue **ones***
Jebakan: *yang merah* → **the red one**, bukan 'the red'.
Tidak ada 'a one' tanpa kata sifat, dan tidak ada *one* untuk kata benda yang tidak bisa dihitung: *some advice*, bukan 'an advice one'.

steps.title: Di kantor dan di toko
steps.text: Perhatikan apa yang digantikan oleh **do so**, **do it**, **one** dan **ones** di setiap kalimat.
steps.body: **one** = satu benda, **ones** = lebih dari satu. **do so** = formal; **do it / do that** = sehari-hari.

steps.title: Kursi untuk ruang rapat
steps.text: Bu Ani sedang memilih kursi untuk ruang rapat baru di sebuah toko furnitur kantor di Surabaya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi ucapan Bu Ani: 'The grey chairs are comfortable, but I prefer the black ___. They match the table.'
options: one
them
ones
question.explanation: *chairs* jamak dan bisa dihitung, dan *They match* menunjukkan lebih dari satu, jadi: **the black ones**. *one* tunggal, dan *them* tidak bisa muncul setelah kata sifat ('the black them' ✗).

steps.title: Hilangkan, tapi sisakan kata kerja bantu
steps.text: Alat terakhir: bicara lebih sedikit. Sisakan satu kata kecil dan hilangkan sisanya.
steps.body:
Setelah **kata kerja bantu** (be, do, did, have, can, will, might, should…), sisakan kata itu dan hilangkan sisanya:
*Are you coming? I **might**.* / *I didn't go, but Rina **did**.*
Setelah **to**, sisakan *to* dan hilangkan kata kerjanya: *I'd like **to**, but I can't.*
Jebakan: 'but I couldn't **do**' ✗ (*tidak bisa* tidak butuh *do*), 'Yes, I'd like.' ✗ → *Yes, I'd like **to***.
Di akhir kalimat, jangan disingkat: *I'm not ready, but Sari **is*** (bukan *Sari's*).

pairs.id: Saya tidak pergi, tapi Rina pergi.

pairs.en: I wanted to help, but I couldn't.
pairs.id: Saya mau bantu, tapi tidak bisa.

pairs.en: I'd like to, but I can't.
I haven't read it, but Pak Hasan has.
pairs.id: Saya belum membacanya, tapi Pak Hasan sudah.

steps.title: Lokakarya hari Sabtu
steps.text: Tim Sari mengajaknya ikut lokakarya hari Sabtu, tapi dia harus mengantar ibunya ke rumah sakit. Hari Senin dia menjelaskan.

options: I wanted to come, but I couldn't.
I wanted to come, but I couldn't do.
I wanted, but I couldn't come.
question.explanation: **I couldn't** sudah cukup: kata kerja bantunya mewakili *couldn't come*. Menambahkan *do* adalah jebakan *tapi tidak bisa*. Dan *want* butuh **to**: *I wanted **to***, bukan *I wanted*.

steps.title: Janji yang ditepati
steps.text: Bu Ani khawatir laporannya akan terlambat. Tapi Rina menepati janjinya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Rina janji mengirim laporannya, dan dia memang mengirimnya.
question.solution: Rina promised to send the report, and she did.
question.explanation: **did** mewakili *sent the report*: sisakan kata kerja bantu bentuk lampau dan hilangkan sisanya. Mengulang *she sent the report* memang benar, tapi berat.

steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk rapat, email atau chat berikutnya!

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Elipsis & substitusi
artifact.intro: Cukup sekali. Ganti kata yang diulang dengan kata pendek (so, not, do so, one, ones), atau hilangkan dan sisakan kata kerja bantu atau to.
rows: think / believe / expect / suppose / guess + so
Is the bank open today? I think so.
I don't think / believe / expect so
Is the meeting cancelled? I don't believe so.
I hope so / I hope not (bukan: I don't hope so)
Will it rain at the wedding? I hope not.
I'm afraid so / I'm afraid not
Is the flight delayed? I'm afraid so.
Do you need a visa? If so, apply early.
do so / did so / has done so
Please do so 24 hours in advance.
The ones on the top shelf are cheaper.
I'd like to, but I can't.
tips: Jangan pakai **yes / no / it** setelah think atau hope: *I think so*, *I hope not*.
Sisakan kata kecilnya: **to** atau **kata kerja bantu**. Tanpa *do* tambahan: *I couldn't* ✓, *I couldn't do* ✗.
**do so** terdengar formal: pakai di pengumuman, laporan dan email; dalam percakapan bilang *do it / do that*.
